pairs.subject: markdown-vault
pairs.evidence: src/features/projects/development/goals/GoalsPage.tsx:60 The goals surface's only contact with the vault is a one-way 'Sync to Obsidian' projection of goals into DevTools/Goals/*.md. Its backend writes a parent wikilink by goal id into notes named by title, and its skip check reads the ledger instead of the disk, so it overwrites human edits without saying so.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/obsidian_brain/mod.rs:1712 The in-band parent link names the goal UUID, but files are named sanitize_filename(title) (mod.rs:1774), so every sub-goal note's parent link resolves to nothing. Renaming a goal also writes a new title-named file and leaves the old note in place; the frontmatter id (mod.rs:1690) is never used to find it.

src-tauri/src/commands/obsidian_brain/mod.rs:1782 The skip check compares the ledger's hash of the last generated content with newly generated content and never reads the file on disk. A note the human deleted stays missing until the goal itself changes, and an edited note is silently replaced when the goal changes. This is a one-way projection that never tells the user that edits are overwritten (the button just says 'Sync to Obsidian', GoalsPage.tsx:109).

src-tauri/src/commands/obsidian_brain/mod.rs:70 The push writes through atomic_write: a .tmp sibling file renamed over the target, with no lock or long-lived handle, so Obsidian never sees a half-written note. Overwriting edits is judged under mirror-indexes.
src/features/projects/development/goals/GoalsPage.tsx:60 This context only pushes; neither its files nor the push command walk the vault (grep of context dirs: no readDir/frontmatter/backlink).
src/features/projects/development/goals/GoalsPage.tsx:60 Goals are read from SQLite, not from the vault, so there is no derived index over vault notes for a read to reconcile.
